source.title: Assessment of the Tayabas Bay fisheries
source.issueMetadata: Philippine Journal of Fisheries 25(1), pages 34-51, January-June 2018

pdfReceipt.retrievalMethod: Unauthenticated official-repository HTTPS download; no login, payment or access-control bypass.

studyScope.reportedStudyWater: Tayabas Bay and adjacent waters of Quezon, Marinduque and Batangas
studyScope.dataCollection: Catch and effort were monitored at the three landing sites; annual yield was raised from those landing centers to the whole bay using gear-count information.
studyScope.recordType: Aggregated historical fisheries landings and stock-assessment context, not georeferenced capture events or a complete waterbody checklist.
speciesRichnessFacts: The article reports 220 fish species in 57 families identified at the three landing sites in 2004.
It reports 230 fish species in 58 families in 2005 and attributes the early increase partly to improved identification capability.
Sixteen selected fish species were used for population-parameter analyses; that selected set is not the complete catch list.

bibliographicAndRightsReview.repeatedPdfRunningFooter: Philippine Journal of Fisheries Volume 24 (1-2), January-December 2017
bibliographicAndRightsReview.currentJournalPolicyStates: Articles submitted to TPJF are licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0; authors retain copyright.
bibliographicAndRightsReview.decision: Keep the complete species list, article figures/tables, and poster-style content out of the public app until the license for this exact 2018 item is confirmed and intended reuse is reviewed. The current journal policy alone is not treated as proof of this archived item's license.

limits: Landing-center data were raised to bay-level estimates; they do not assign each species to a precise capture point or establish a georeferenced occurrence at each landing site.
The study includes adjacent waters as part of its assessment context, so it is not a clean station-by-station attribution to the current mapped Bay lead.
The study period ended in 2013 and does not establish current species presence or abundance.
The article's count of species identified changed alongside reported improvements in identification capability, so richness counts are not directly interpreted as ecological trend.
The printed 2018 issue metadata and repeated 2017 running footer conflict; retain the repository/DOI issue record and flag the PDF pagination/header anomaly.
Tayabas Bay is shared across Quezon, Batangas and Marinduque; no legal boundary or municipal-water polygon is derived from the paper's descriptive study area.
nextAction: Confirm the exact 2018 article's item-level license or permission and evaluate its source-specific taxonomy and catch-scope fields before extracting the selected taxa into a licensed research projection; continue to seek station-resolved and freshwater records separately.
